## 0. Facts

XLY **−0.77%** (open **111.89** → close **111.50**). Implied prior close ~**112.36**. Path: **gap/open already red after 8:30 ET CPI**, then a further grind lower into the close (not a reversal). SPY **−1.08%**. Relative **+0.32%** — down with the tape, **outperformed SPY**.

Direction **down**, magnitude **mild** (sub-1% ETF; SPY itself was closer to notable).

---

## 1. What drove the sector

Taxonomy: **S0 shared-macro CPI binary resolved hawkish**, transmitted through **duration/growth beta (AMZN/TSLA sleeve)** more than through a broad consumer-health wipeout. **S1 gasoline** showed up in the *print* (September CPI gasoline **+9.1% m/m**), not in the morning’s *live* oil tape. **S2** was a defensive rotation (staples/healthcare up, tech crushed), not discretionary expansion. **S4** 1d relative stayed modestly positive.

**CLAIM:** September CPI (released 8:30 ET Oct 14) was hot on core and slightly hot on headline YoY; energy/gasoline dominated the m/m headline.
**URL:** https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/14/cpi-inflation-report-september-2026.html
**PUBLISHED:** 2026-10-14
**QUOTE:** “The consumer price index … rose a seasonally adjusted 0.6% for the month, putting the 12-month rate at 3.7% … Economists surveyed by Dow Jones expected respective gains of 0.6% and 3.6%. … core CPI rose 0.3% for the month and was up 2.6% … compared with respective estimates for 0.2% and 2.5%. … Gasoline prices soared 9.1%, accounting for about half the gain in headline CPI.”
**SUMMARY:** Headline in line m/m / hot YoY; **core miss** (0.3/2.6 vs 0.2/2.5). Energy **+5.2% m/m**. This was the session’s signed object.

**CLAIM:** Equities sold off on hike repricing; S&P ~−1.1%, Nasdaq ~−1.9%, Dow ~−0.1%; 10Y spiked then faded.
**URL:** https://www.latimes.com/business/story/2026-10-14/stocks-drop-to-their-worst-day-since-july-as-inflation-worsens
**PUBLISHED:** 2026-10-14
**QUOTE:** “The Standard & Poor’s 500 index sank 1.1% … The Dow Jones industrial average fell 0.1%, and the Nasdaq composite slid 1.9% as stocks in the artificial intelligence industry led the way lower. … 10-year Treasury … yield briefly jump above 5.32% from less than 5.17% just before the inflation report’s release.”
**SUMMARY:** Risk-off was **AI/growth/duration**, not equal-weight consumer collapse. Matches SPY −1.08% vs XLY −0.77%.

**CLAIM:** XLY internals were a barbell: AMZN/TSLA down more than the ETF; HD held/green.
**URL:** https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-amazoncom-nasdaq-amzn-stock-falls-17-heres-what-happened-2026-10-14/
**PUBLISHED:** 2026-10-14
**QUOTE:** “Shares of Amazon.com, Inc. were down 1.7% … last traded at $254.08. … The stock had previously closed at $258.58.”
**SUMMARY:** AMZN ~**−1.7%** (XLY’s ~23% weight) was a primary drag.

**CLAIM:** Tesla underperformed the ETF.
**URL:** https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-tesla-nasdaq-tsla-shares-down-22-heres-what-happened-2026-10-14/
**PUBLISHED:** 2026-10-14
**QUOTE:** “Tesla, Inc. fell 2.2% on Wednesday. … last traded at $367.16. … previously closed at $375.23.”
**SUMMARY:** TSLA ~**−2.2%** (~18% of XLY) was the other megacap drag. Combined AMZN+TSLA ~40% of XLY explains most of the ETF’s decline without needing a retail-sales shock.

**CLAIM:** Home Depot did not participate in the growth selloff.
**URL:** https://www.techi.com/quote/HD/historical/
**PUBLISHED:** 2026-10-14 close data
**QUOTE:** Close **$295.51**, **+0.54%**.
**SUMMARY:** HD (~5% of XLY) was a **cushion**, not a consumer-cyclical wrecking ball.

**CLAIM:** Sector rotation was defensive vs growth, not “discretionary uniquely broken.”
**URL:** https://www.thetrading.tools/sector-performance
**PUBLISHED:** post-close 2026-10-14 (pipeline/table)
**QUOTE:** XLK **−2.98%**; XLP **+2.22%**; XLE **+0.68%**; XLY ~**−0.75/−0.77%**; only 3 of 11 sectors higher; healthcare ~**+2.5%**.
**SUMMARY:** XLY sat **between SPY and XLK**: down, but not the dump. Staples/healthcare absorbed the CPI shock; tech took the duration hit.

---

## 2. Audit morning S0–S4 vs reality

Use **morning numbers**, not post-close rewrites.

| Sleeve | Morning | Reality | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **S0 shared macro** | **0, unsigned.** CPI is a *distribution*; do not pre-score (10-02). Hawkish skew in consensus, miss would break hike repricing. ES/NQ inside ±0.5%. | CPI **resolved hawkish on core**; hike odds jumped (CNBC: ~54% Oct hike on FedWatch; LA Times: ~35% vs 22% prior). SPY −1.08%. | **Process right, realization hawkish.** Not a missed signed lean — it was an unprinted binary that printed hot. |
| **S1 spine** | **0.** No retail/claims/confidence. Gasoline spike **off** (WTI −1.59%, RBOB −0.54%). Credit 1d flat. | CPI gasoline **+9.1% m/m**, energy **+5.2%** — September *lagged* pump, not live WTI. No same-day retail print. HD green, AMZN/TSLA duration-red. | **Live-oil S1=0 was contemporaneously honest and still the wrong object vs the 8:30 print.** Gasoline-in-CPI was the sector factor that fired. |
| **S2 breadth** | **0.** XLY PM **−0.01%**, mid-board. XLK already lagging pre-open. | Post-print: defensives lead, XLK −3%, XLY mid-red. No discretionary-specific expansion. | **Pre-open flat was correct.** Breadth after 8:30 was **rotation**, not XLY idiosyncratic failure. |
| **S3 flows** | **0.** Contango, HY OAS flat, pre-CPI hedged/neutral. | VIX up (X posts ~16.87, ~+10%); no liquidation cascade in XLY. Volume on XLY elevated (~8.3m) but AMZN/TSLA volume was actually *below* average in MarketBeat midday prints. | **Mostly holds.** Risk-off, not a positioning blow-up in discretionary. |
| **S4 tape** | **0.** 1d rel **+0.09%** sub-gate; 1w rel +0.71%; 1m rel **−2.72%**. Confirmation-only. | Close rel **+0.32%**. Still beating SPY. 1m lag not “cured.” | **Correct as confirmation-only.** Relative catch-up vs SPY continued *through a down day*. |

**Pipeline vs card:** LLM leading sum **all-zero**, leftover-anchor flatten (09-21) **binds**, “do not mint direction from tape_anchor/index_carry,” **band stays flat**, confidence 0.4. Deterministic engine still emitted **down/mild** via `index_carry −0.411` (general −1.645) + tape_anchor 0.224, `calendar_size_gate=True`, total **−0.187**.

**Actual = down/mild.** Direction/band **hit**, but the **engine hit was leftover carry, not a scored CPI call**. The card’s “stay flat” was the honest pre-print; the binary then delivered the down tape the carry had already guessed.

---

## 3. Interactions / double-count / knowable-at-open

- **Do not double-count CPI as both “market down” and “XLY down.”** S0 explains SPY −1.08%. Sector residual is **rel +0.32%**. Discretionary was **not the shock’s epicenter**; XLK was.
- **Gasoline double-count trap:** Morning **live WTI relief** and **CPI gasoline +9.1%** are different clocks. Scoring S1=0 from live oil did **not** contradict a hot *September* gasoline CPI. Carrying 10-13 oil shock forward was correctly forbidden; **ignoring the CPI gasoline *distribution*** underweighted S1’s two-sided tail.
- **AMZN/TSLA vs “consumer health”:** Morning said score broad consumer, not two names. Reality: **two names did most of the damage**; HD/MCD-type sleeves did not confirm a wallet shock. Treating XLY as consumer-health would have **over-explained** a duration/AI-adjacent beta move.
- **Knowable at open:** CPI **date, size_gate, two-sidedness, XLK already lagging, XLY PM dead flat** — yes. **Core 0.3 vs 0.2, hike-odds jump, AMZN −1.7 / TSLA −2.2 vs HD +0.5, XLK −3** — no. September fuel *levels* were knowable; the **print’s core miss** was not.

**KNOWABLE_AT_OPEN: partially.**

---

## 4. Outliers inside the sector

- **TSLA ~−2.2%** and **AMZN ~−1.7%**: duration/growth, larger than XLY.
- **HD +0.54%**: opposite sign; housing/retail did not confirm CPI-as-consumer-crunch.
- **XLP +2.22% vs XLY −0.77%**: intra-consumer **staples over cyclical** — the clean sector-relative tell.
- **XLY vs SPY +32 bp**: outlier vs a “cyclicals get destroyed on hot CPI” cartoon; the cartoon belonged to **XLK/AI**.
